title: Rama: Accepting the Exile
subtitle: A royal command, a kingdom, and a promise

acceptance.author: Valmiki
acceptance.locator: Ayodhyakandam · Section XIX; Ayodhyakandam · Section XIX, normalized characters 896-1042
acceptance.excerpt: What of the command of the king, my father, I shall even at thy mandate joyfully make over unto Bharata, my kingdom, Sita, wealth and even my life
acceptance.note: Verbatim English translation from Dutt. The Mahabharata volume is a condensed verse rendering; the Ramayana volume contains only the Balakandam and Ayodhyakandam.

duration.author: Valmiki
duration.locator: Ayodhyakandam · Section XIX; Ayodhyakandam · Section XIX, normalized characters 1348-1472
duration.excerpt: I shall, not even judging the propriety of my father's words, speedily repair unto the forest of Dandaka for fourteen years.
duration.note: Verbatim English translation from Dutt. The Mahabharata volume is a condensed verse rendering; the Ramayana volume contains only the Balakandam and Ayodhyakandam.

narrativeBlocks.title: The command changes the succession
narrativeBlocks.body: In Manmatha Nath Dutt's prose translation of the Ayodhyakandam, Rama responds to the command that sends him to the forest for fourteen years while Bharata is to receive the kingdom.

narrativeBlocks.title: Rama accepts the command
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (Dutt's English rendering; whitespace normalized): “What of the command of the king, my father, I shall even at thy mandate joyfully make over unto Bharata, my kingdom, Sita, wealth and even my life”

narrativeBlocks.title: The promise is more than a throne
narrativeBlocks.body: Rama says he will give up kingdom, Sita, wealth, and even life at the command of his father and Kaikeyi. The words are part of this translation's literary scene.

narrativeBlocks.title: A specific volume and translation
narrativeBlocks.body: This source is Volume 1 of Dutt's English prose translation, containing the Balakandam and Ayodhyakandam. It does not include every later Ramayana episode or regional retelling.

narrativeBlocks.title: Exile begins with a decision
narrativeBlocks.body: The passage frames the exile through Rama's response to a royal promise and command, not through a single general definition of duty.
